subject: Redwood DPA & data handling items — follow-up from today's call
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@aurora-tech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood DPA & data handling items — follow-up from today's call

Alex —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed on the call:

- Scope: Aurora is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing recommendation and support flows (PII in prompts, customer IDs, and embeddings).
- Primary asks from your side: controller/processor roles, subprocessors, breach notification timing, data residency options, and retention/logging controls.

Answers / notes:
1) Controller vs Processor: For typical deployments Aurora will be the Controller of customer data you provide; Redwood will process that data on your behalf as a Processor under the DPA. We can add language for any specific case where Aurora wants to assert additional responsibilities.

2) Subprocessors: We maintain a current list of subprocessors and attach it to the DPA. We disclose any new subprocessors by email and provide a 30-day review/objection window per the DPA. If Aurora objects and we can’t reach an agreement, the standard remedy in the DPA is the ability to terminate that portion of the service.

3) Breach notice: Our standard commitment is to notify customers of confirmed security incidents affecting customer data within 72 hours of becoming aware, along with an initial summary and planned remediation steps. We can add an escalation path to include Aurora’s security contact for high-severity incidents.

4) Data residency & retention: We support region-specific hosting for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API usage we offer EU-only processing in our EU region for customers requiring residency (subject to capacity). Logging and access logs retention defaults to 90 days; we can discuss longer retention or shorter retention windows and include controls in the contract.

Next steps (action items):
- I’ve attached the current DPA and subprocessors list (see attachments).
- Please confirm if Aurora needs EU-only processing for all production traffic or just for a subset.
- If you have specific retention windows for logs/requests, send those numbers and I’ll loop in Product/Infra.
- If the legal team wants to redline the DPA, please send their markups; our legal team (cc Marissa) will review.

Attaching: DPA_Redwood_20270428.pdf; subprocessors_list_20270428.csv

Best,
Ben

Ben —

Thanks for the follow-up and the materials. A few clarifying questions from legal/privacy:

- Can you confirm in plain language whether Aurora (as the customer) will always be controller and Redwood will always be processor?
- For subprocessors: do you allow customers to approve or block specific subprocessors, and what’s the exact objection process/timing?
- Breach notices: Aurora needs an initial notification within 48 hours for incidents impacting PII. Is there flexibility on the 72-hour commit you mentioned?
- Data residency: we need EU-only processing for all EU customer traffic — is that supported for Hosted or would we need Dedicated?
- Logging/retention: we will likely request a 30-day maximum retention for request payloads containing PII. Is that configurable?

If legal prefers, we can send a short redline of the DPA.

Appreciate the quick turn here — looking to close the procurement cycle fast.

—Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-02T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA & data handling items — follow-up from today's call

Alex —

Thanks — answers inline below. I’ll also ask Legal to review if you send a redline.

> Can you confirm in plain language whether Aurora (as the customer) will always be controller and Redwood will always be processor?
Yes — in the common SaaS deployment Aurora is the Controller of the customer data you provide. Redwood processes that data on your instructions and is therefore a Processor under the DPA. We can add clause language to make that explicit.

> For subprocessors: do you allow customers to approve or block specific subprocessors, and what’s the exact objection process/timing?
We maintain a published subprocessors list (attached). We notify customers of new subprocessors by email and provide a 30-day review/objection window. If Aurora objects, we will engage to understand the concern; mutually agreeable mitigation is preferred. If we can’t reach agreement, the available contractual remedy is termination of the affected services (per the DPA).

> Breach notices: Aurora needs an initial notification within 48 hours for incidents impacting PII. Is there flexibility on the 72-hour commit you mentioned?
Our standard is 72 hours, which aligns with our incident verification process and coordination with engineering. I don’t want to promise 48 hours without Legal/SEC approval; however, we can offer an enhanced SLA for high-severity incidents that includes a named Redwood escalation contact and a commitment to provide initial findings as soon as practicable. I’ve cc’d Marissa from Legal to weigh in on whether we can move to 48 hours for this deal.

> Data residency: we need EU-only processing for all EU customer traffic — is that supported for Hosted or would we need Dedicated?
We support EU-only processing for Hosted customers via our EU region (we can route traffic and data storage to the EU). For strict contractual residency guarantees or for higher isolation, Dedicated is the recommended option. I’ll have Product/Infra confirm capacity for EU hosting for the expected volumes.

> Logging/retention: we will likely request a 30-day maximum retention for request payloads containing PII. Is that configurable?
Default logging retention is 90 days. We can support shorter retention windows for request payloads and logs as a configuration/policy for your account; we’ll need to validate based on the deployment mode. Please send the specific retention numbers and which categories (request payloads, audit logs, access logs) and we’ll map feasibility.

Next steps:
- If Aurora sends a redline we’ll prioritize Legal review.
- Marissa — can you confirm whether we can offer a 48-hour initial notice commitment for this customer or if 72 remains required?
- Alex — please confirm whether you require Hosted EU-only processing or Dedicated.

Thanks,
Ben
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Redwood DPA & data handling items — Aurora Tech (legal/ops questions)

Marissa / Rachel —

Forwarding Aurora thread — they pushed on 48-hour breach notification and require EU-only processing for EU traffic. Key asks:
- Can Legal sign up to a 48-hour initial notification for PII incidents for this deal?
- Product/Infra: can we guarantee EU-only processing on Hosted (not Dedicated) for the expected volumes (pilot ~10k requests/day, 100k/month)?
- Ops: can we support a 30-day max retention for request payloads containing PII?

Attachments in the original include our DPA and subprocessor list. Alex indicated legal could send a redline; if they do we should aim to turn within 3 business days.

Proposed approach: keep our standard 72-hour notice in the DPA but offer an escalation path and named contact for Aurora; confirm Hosted EU-region availability; offer configurable retention to 30 days if Ops confirms. If Legal signs off, we’ll accept their redlines where they don't materially increase risk; otherwise escalate to Kate (GC).

Thoughts? I’m happy to setup a quick sync between you and Aurora legal if that helps move things faster.

Best,
Ben
(end of thread)
